How can I turn a mono signal into stereo in a channel in ?

Short answer: the channel is already stereo and carries the same signal twice, so the work is making the left differ from the right. Utility's Width knob will not do it. Reach for a device that puts a different signal on each side: Delay with Stereo Link off and unequal left and right times, Chorus-Ensemble, a reverb, or an Audio Effect Rack holding two chains panned hard apart with a few milliseconds of delay on one of them.

from Mono/Stereo Conversions: "Signals in the track's device chain are always stereo, even when the track's input is mono or when the track plays mono samples. Mono is turned into stereo simply by using the identical signal for left and right channels."

A mono sample, a mono input and a mono synth all reach the device chain as two identical channels. Stereo is whatever difference you put between them.

Width scales the side component, which is the difference between left and right. Identical channels have no difference, so the knob sweeps with nothing to scale.

A track records mono samples when its Input Channel is a mono input, so a two-channel source arriving on one input stays mono for good. Choosing a stereo pair records both sides. Which hardware inputs appear as mono and which as stereo pairs is set in the Channel Configuration dialog in the audio settings.

00:00 In this video, we're going to take a look at linked tracks. Using the Link Track feature allows you to adjust multiple tracks to edit or adjust parameters. A great use for this feature is when you've recorded multiple sources at the same time.

00:17 So for example, in this case, I have a multi mic recording of some drums in this project. Linking tracks is a very simple procedure in the arrangement view. All I have to do is select the tracks I'd like to link together,

00:33 right click to access the context menu and select Link Tracks. When tracks have been successfully linked together, there's a small icon indicating linked tracks in the top right-hand corner of each track.

00:46 Now, if I go into my Arrangement View and select any of the clips from the linked tracks, all of the linked tracks are highlighted. With the tracks linked, you can now perform all kinds of edits to all the linked tracks. For example... Splitting and deleting selections.

01:13 Reversing selections. Or adding cross-fades and fades. And even renaming selections. You can also manipulate warp markers and warp parameters of all linked tracks. Another great feature of Linked Tracks is the ability to adjust parameters in the mixer section.

01:56 By selecting one of the tracks in a Link Track selection, you're able to adjust the mixer parameters of that particular track. In this state, you can continue to work on other individual tracks and adjust their mixer parameters.

02:20 If you wish to work on all of the linked tracks at the same time, simply click on the Link Track icon and adjust their parameters. This allows for a great amount of flexibility for you to either adjust individual parameters in the mixer section,

02:37 or adjust them all collectively together. Not only can you link together Audio tracks, but you can also link together MIDI tracks. or a combination of MIDI and Audio tracks. As a final technique, Link Tracks can also be used to comp together
03:04 several takes from several tracks simultaneously.

recalls MicroFreak presets 401 and 402, sequencer patterns A and B, short five-step sequences, paraphonic playing, and a change from the Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/04 Harmo to Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/06 VAnalog. The log does not pin either preset to an exact passage.

The Launchpad/UG/05 Session Mode controlled Live's pan, send, volume, record arm, stop clip, click, device, tap tempo, and fixed-length recording. The Launchpad/UG/09 Sequencer was not used; the sequences came from the Microfreak/UG/13 Sequencer.

Sparse notes give way to sweeps of filter cutoff (CC 23, reaching 91), resonance (CC 83, reaching 74), filter amount (CC 26, reaching 84), and oscillator timbre, wave, and shape (CC 12, 10, 13); see Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values. The note count thins after 02:00 while those oscillator controls keep moving. The session log identifies the opening sound as Harmo, though the MIDI does not encode the loaded preset.

Cycling envelope rise (CC 102) appears around 03:33. LFO sync rate (CC 94) changes around 04:33; the log recalls changing the LFO shape from sine to saw, but that waveform choice is not present in the CC capture. Spice (CC 2) begins around 06:24 and moves through values up to 82 during a denser run of notes. Around 09:34, a brief group of sequencer sync-rate changes (CC 92, up to 102) accompanies the transition into a quieter passage. See Microfreak/UG/13 Sequencer/01 Use/01 Select & Play for switching patterns A and B.

Pitch-bend messages return around 10:00 and continue through the middle of the recording. Cycling envelope amount (CC 24) enters around 12:10 and reaches 127. The log recalls routing cycling envelope and keyboard pressure to pitch through the Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations; the MIDI records the bend and envelope controls but cannot establish that internal routing. Oscillator type (CC 9) changes around 14:49, while the saved sound at that instant is unknown. Around 17:00, cycling envelope fall (CC 103), hold (CC 28), and rise (CC 102) changes join the filter sweeps.

Long passages of cutoff and resonance movement, continuing pitch bend, and fewer notes make the middle more droning. From about 22:00, the note activity increases along with Spice, oscillator shape, timbre, and wave changes. Glide (CC 5) appears at 23:44 and rises as high as 31 in the final minutes. A further oscillator-type change (CC 9) occurs near 26:30; the log says the session ended on V.Analog, but the CC value alone does not identify that oscillator model.

These times follow the Ableton arrangement at a constant 56.818 BPM. The captured MIDI contains note and controller events from the “mf MIDI ALL” track. Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values identifies the controls; the GitP/A/Session/26/10/11-Sun/Asset/MIDI/Full/mid preserves their recorded values for inspection.
